### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **20** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ai.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-chatbot.mdx`  _(via DRAFT_REVIEW_PART_TYPE (symbol, a top-level const object), DraftReviewListParsed (symbol, a top-level type), DraftReviewListSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/data-service.mdx`  _(via /api/protocol.zod (route, a path literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via /api/protocol.zod (route, a path literal on a changed line))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ai.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e06729a9b8b99b5b6c3e3b512e48fefb61938d9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e73580db61d84de5f2bcaf306a59e10c4a825066` — the merge of head `3a44ab65ad421afb684e06cf8fc4faf3253e76c8` into base `6e06729a9b8b99b5b6c3e3b512e48fefb61938d9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e73580db61d84de5f2bcaf306a59e10c4a825066 && git checkout e73580db61d84de5f2bcaf306a59e10c4a825066
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6e06729a9b8b99b5b6c3e3b512e48fefb61938d9 3a44ab65ad421afb684e06cf8fc4faf3253e76c8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6e06729a9b8b99b5b6c3e3b512e48fefb61938d9 && git merge --no-ff 3a44ab65ad421afb684e06cf8fc4faf3253e76c8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e06729a9b8b99b5b6c3e3b512e48fefb61938d9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6e06729a9b8b99b5b6c3e3b512e48fefb61938d9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### Contract review brief — PR #38102 @ `fb2070cdafd27c0d61117c5db285e3bdd382b183` (card #38048)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths packages/spec/src/ai/draft-review.zod.ts packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #38048: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #38102: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `fb2070cdafd27c0d61117c5db285e3bdd382b183`
  · the check-runs on `fb2070cdafd27c0d61117c5db285e3bdd382b183`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: packages/spec/src/ai/draft-review.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `SCRATCHPAD/pr-38102/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fb2070cdafd27c0d61117c5db285e3bdd382b183`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/draft-review.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts + ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/mapMessages.ts, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/chat/DraftReviewCard.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/chat/draftReviewGroups.ts, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/chat/types.ts, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/chatMessageAdapter.ts, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/ChatbotEnhanced.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/index.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/ChatPane.tsx

This record covers `fb2070cda` only. The PR head has since moved to `98b52b0a6` (one commit, one line: `Metadata-protocol: none` to `added` in `.changeset/38048-draft-review-part.md`); that head is not covered here.

Remainder, the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT: the two test files under `plugin-chatbot/src/__tests__`, `packages/spec/src/ai/draft-review.test.ts`, the eleven locale packs, the README and mdx prose, the generated spec artifacts, `llms.txt` and the changesets' prose.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface, `@objectstack/spec/ai`: right.** `index.ts` adds one `export *`. New names: `DRAFT_REVIEW_PART_TYPE`, `DRAFT_REVIEW_MAX`, five schemas (`DraftReviewList`, `DraftReviewItem`, `DraftReviewVerdict`, `DraftReviewVerdictRefusal`, `DraftReviewLinks`) and their input and `Parsed` types. `api-surface/ai.json` gains 17 rows and `json-schema.manifest/ai.json` gains 5, which matches. Nothing existing changes.
- **Accept set, part `data`: right against the card and amendment 7232366780.** The card's sketch is `{ drafts[], omitted? }` with rows `{ type, name, package, label?, verdict | null, verdictWithheld?, verdictError?, verdictRead, review { changes, item } }`, at most 50. The schema is that shape. Its five tightenings are the ones the amendment and report 7232350452 state: `verdict` required (nullable), `review` closed at two keys, `drafts` at least 1, `omitted` an integer of at least 1, both links pattern-checked. The card allows refinement if stated on the card before merge; it is stated.
- **Closure: right for the five new objects, wrong as the changeset words it.** All five are `strictObject`. The rows of `refusals` and `advisories` are `RuntimeAuthoringIssueSchema`, which is a plain `z.object` (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts:1078`): an unknown key there is dropped, not refused. See N1.
- **Accept set, review links: wrong.** The pattern admits values a browser resolves to another host. See S1.
- **Authorable-surface shard, 19 rows: right as generated.** The five closed objects contribute 9 + 2 + 2 + 3 + 3 keys. The ratchet reads this as a metadata-protocol change; see ②.
- **Public surface, `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot`: right.** It exports `DraftReviewCard`, `DraftReviewCardProps` and `extractDraftReview`; `ChatbotEnhancedProps` gains the optional `onOpenReviewLink` and `reviewLinkHref`; `ChatbotEnhancedMessage` gains the optional `draftReview`. All are additive and the changeset names each one.
- **Gates at this head: not answered.** `Check Changeset` failed (see ②). `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test UI` failed only because their lanes were cancelled when the head moved: 28 runs are `cancelled`, including every `Test Core` shard, `Type Check · workspace`, `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI` and `Build Core`. Green at this head: `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`. So the derived gate families have no verdict on `fb2070cda`.

### ② Semver level

M1 (must-fix) — the declaration at this head is wrong. `.changeset/38048-draft-review-part.md` and the PR body both say `Metadata-protocol: none`, and `Check Changeset` (run 140833349986) is red on it: `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json` moved, so the line must be `added`, `narrowed` or `semantic`, with the package at least `minor`.

- The right value is `Metadata-protocol: added`. The rows are new keys only and nothing is removed or re-meant. It is also the precedent: `.changeset/37872-ask-question-envelope.md` on `main` (#37930) is `'@objectstack/spec': minor` with `Metadata-protocol: added` for the same kind of change, a new closed stream shape in `@objectstack/spec/ai`.
- `'@objectstack/spec': minor` is right: new exports, nothing narrowed.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right on both changesets.
- The UI changeset (`plugin-chatbot`, `app-shell`, `i18n` at `patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none`) is right. It follows `.changeset/37873-question-card.md` on `main`, which ships new `plugin-chatbot` exports at `patch`, and it touches no spec shard.
- Claim comment 7232385588 already amends the claim to `added`, and `98b52b0a6` changes the changeset line. The PR body still read `none` when I read it; it must say `added` as well.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, surface beyond the claim (`chatMessageAdapter.ts`, `draftReviewGroups.ts`, a second test file, `reviewLinkHref`, `llms.txt`): accepted. Each is in amendment 7232366780, and each is read in ④ or sits in the remainder.
- Deviation, overflow in the eleven locales not measured in a browser: not answered by this review. It is a card acceptance line and belongs to the lane seat's ACCEPT; nothing in the diff measures it.
- Deviation, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally and left to CI: still open at this head, because the CI lane that runs it was cancelled.
- Deviation, branch name `claude/project-thread-qdbmce`: matches the claim.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff has no query, no id materialisation and no join.
- `security_findings: none` in the report does not hold; see S1.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ai/draft-review.zod.ts`**

S1 (should-fix) — the Console-path pattern does not keep a link on the site. `consolePath` is `/^\/(?!\/)/`: it checks the first two characters and nothing after them. Its own comment says it exists so that a link is "never `//` (which a browser reads as another host)", and the PR body says it refuses protocol-relative values "since the card renders them as anchors". Two values pass it and still resolve to another host under the WHATWG URL rules for http and https:
- a slash followed by a backslash, as in `/\evil.example/x`: a backslash is read as a slash, so this is the protocol-relative form;
- a slash, a tab or newline, then a slash: the parser removes tabs and newlines before it parses, which leaves `//evil.example/x`.

The card puts the value into the anchor's `href` as it is (`DraftReviewCard.tsx`, `link`). `ChatPane` builds the href with `documentHref(useHref('/'), path)`, which on a root mount returns the path unchanged, and hands the same string to `navigate` on a plain click. I did not read what `react-router` does with it. `draft-review.test.ts` covers `https:`, `//`, `javascript:`, a relative path and the empty string, and neither of these.

What holds: `javascript:` and every other scheme are refused, since the value must start with `/`. A crafted `type`, `name` or `package` cannot produce either bypass through the door's builders: `studioChangesReviewLink` and `studioItemReviewLink` (`packages/types/src/studio-review-links.ts:22-29`) pass each segment through `encodeURIComponent`, which encodes slash, backslash, `?`, `#` and control characters. A name of `..` survives encoding and a browser folds the dot segment, but the result stays on the same origin. So the hole is open only to a producer that does not use the builders, and the grade is should-fix, not must-fix. It is a finding on the contract because the schema is the reader's only guard, the reader is told to add no second parser, and the objects are published closed from day one, so tightening the pattern after release is a narrowing. The fix is in the pattern: refuse a backslash, whitespace and control characters anywhere in the value (or anchor it to the `/studio/` prefix both builders emit), and add both values to the refusal test.

S2 (should-fix) — the contract does not say whether a draft saved twice in one turn is one row or two. `drafts` is described as "The saved drafts, in save order", and the module text says "the drafts one ask turn saved". A build turn commonly saves the same item more than once. The reader assumes one row per draft: `DraftReviewCard.tsx` keys each row by `type:name` inside its package group, so two rows for one draft collide on the React key, and both count toward the cap of 50 and toward `omitted`. cloud#5172 cannot be read from here, so the text is all its author has. State it in the `drafts` description: one row per draft, unique by package, type and name, placed at its first (or last) save.

Q1, shape against the card and the amendment: holds, apart from S1. The limits are right: 1 to 50 rows, `omitted` an integer of at least 1, non-empty `type`, `name`, `package` and `label`, `verdictRead` a two-value enum.

Q2, reuse of `RuntimeAuthoringIssueSchema`: sound, and real. `refusals` and `advisories` are `z.array(RuntimeAuthoringIssueSchema)`, imported from `../api/protocol.zod`; nothing is copied. An `ai` file importing from `api` has precedent (`dataset-tools.zod.ts:10` on `main`). It is the shape the door answers: `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.ts:1425-1433` returns `{ publishable: refusals.length === 0, refusals, advisories }`. `DraftReviewVerdictRefusalSchema` does not reuse it and should not: it is the door's error `{ code, message, status }` for a verdict that was not read, which is a different thing from a finding, and the seat's ruling names `refusals` and `advisories` only.

Q6, as a contract for cloud#5172: the shape in report 7232350452 agrees with the schema key for key, and the generated reference page carries the module text (producer, timing before `finish`, one part, save order, `verdict` null with its two reasons, the two builders by name). A producer that follows the report passes the parse. The gaps are S2, N2 and N3.

**`packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts`**: holds. One `export *` and one line in the module list.

**`ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/mapMessages.ts`**: agrees with the contract. `extractDraftReview` selects by `DRAFT_REVIEW_PART_TYPE` and reads `part.data` through `DraftReviewListSchema.safeParse` only; there is no second parser and no hand-read field. A refused part returns `undefined`, `uiMessageToChatMessage` then omits `draftReview`, and nothing throws (Q3). It takes the last part of that type, which is right for a stream that replaces a part by id.

**Live only (Q5)**: true in the console, and it is what the card asks (ruling Q2 = A). The part is not in `STORED_ANSWER_DATA_PARTS` (`toolResultParsers.ts:324-333`, unchanged). All three rebuild paths go through that allow-list: `storedAnswerData` in `aiChatHydration.ts:173`, `storedAnswerParts` in `useChatConversation.ts:396` (the browser cache) and in `useObjectChat.ts:794` (the store rebuild). None of them names `draftReview`. `chatMessageAdapter.ts` adds it to `RuntimeOnlyMessageKeys`, which keeps it out of the authored message type. The UI test pins both the allow-list and `storedAnswerData`.

**`DraftReviewCard.tsx`, `draftReviewGroups.ts`, `ChatbotEnhanced.tsx`, `types.ts`, `index.tsx`**: agree with the card. One row per draft with label or name, type, a verdict badge and a Review link to `review.item`; one "Review and publish" link per package to `review.changes`; `omitted` as "+N more"; no button of any kind. Both files type against the `Parsed` types from the spec and read no field the schema does not declare. Every link has an `aria-label` and the section is labelled by its title.

**`ChatPane.tsx`**: agrees. A plain left click goes to `navigate(path)`, so the live card survives; a modified or middle click keeps the anchor's href, which carries the router basename. Subject to S1.

Nits, none of which changes the verdict:

- N1 (nit) — "Every level is closed: an unknown key is refused, never dropped" (changeset, PR body, test header) is not true of the rows inside `refusals` and `advisories`, which are a plain `z.object` and drop unknown keys. The behaviour is the better one, since a new field on the door's finding does not blank the card; the sentence should say the five new objects are closed.
- N2 (nit) — the descriptions state three invariants the schema does not enforce: `publishable` is true exactly when `refusals` is empty; `verdictWithheld` or `verdictError` is present only when `verdict` is null; `omitted` is present only when 50 rows are listed. The card draws `publishable: false` with no refusals as "0 problems", and `publishable: true` with refusals as "Will publish". The door derives `publishable` itself, so this needs a producer that departs from the door.
- N3 (nit) — the part id `draft-review` appears only in the card, the report and the PR body. The reader's own comment depends on it ("With a stable part id the stream keeps one part"). The spec could export it or name it in the module text; the citations part has the same gap.
- N4 (nit) — "a conversation reloaded from history shows no card" is written in the spec as a property of the part, but it is a property of this console's rebuild paths and of the producer not storing the part. `uiMessageToChatMessage` draws the card from any message whose parts carry it, and `useObjectChat` passes `initialMessages` that already have `parts` through unchanged.
- N5 (nit) — `DraftReviewVerdictRefusal` sits next to `verdict.refusals` and means something else (the door's error, not a publish refusal). The name is published now and costs a rename later.

Not read: objectstack-ai/cloud#5172 (the producer), and `react-router`'s handling of the S1 values in `navigate`.

## 席位核对 — L1 @ `98b52b0a68ffc2ad2757e7dde78fd1c385207c45`

**Verdict: REVISE.** Three items, all small and all in `packages/spec/src/ai/draft-review.zod.ts`, its test and the changeset prose. The rest of the PR holds.

Contract review: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER (published schema under `packages/spec/src/**`). Record 7232434714 at `fb2070cd` is FAIL on M1 with S1 and S2 open. This L1 verdict adopts S1, S2 and N1 as required changes; N2–N5 stay nits.

### M1 — closed at this head

`98b52b0a6` changes the changeset line to `Metadata-protocol: added`, and the body now reads `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `Metadata-protocol: added`. The red `Check Changeset` in this head's check-runs is the `synchronize` run (02:28:59Z), which read the body before it was edited. The `edited` run of `PR Automation` (02:30:57Z) passed. `'@objectstack/spec': minor` with `added` follows `.changeset/37872-ask-question-envelope.md` on `main`.

### Required

- **R1 (S1). Make `consolePath` refuse a link that leaves the site.** `/^\/(?!\/)/` checks only the first two characters. `/\evil.example/x` passes and a browser reads `/\` as `//`. A slash, then a tab or newline, then a slash also passes, and the URL parser strips the tab or newline first. Both go unchanged into the card's anchor `href` and into `navigate(path)` in `ChatPane.tsx:287`. The module comment and the PR body both promise "never `//`", so the schema is wrong against its own words. The objects ship closed from day one, so tightening this after release would be a narrowing. Fix it now. Refuse a backslash, whitespace and C0 control characters anywhere in the value, or anchor the pattern to the `/studio/` prefix that both builders in `packages/types/src/studio-review-links.ts` emit. Add `/\evil.example/x` and `/\t/evil.example/x` (a real tab) to the refusal rows in `draft-review.test.ts`, and keep a builder-made link in the accept rows.
- **R2 (S2). Say what a draft saved twice is.** `drafts` says "The saved drafts, in save order". A build turn often saves the same item more than once, and the card keys rows by `type:name` inside a package group, so two rows for one draft collide and both count toward the 50 cap and `omitted`. cloud#5172 has only this text to go on. Write it into the `drafts` description, for example: one row per draft, unique by `package`, `type` and `name`, placed at its first save, carrying the latest verdict. Regenerate the reference page and `llms.txt` if they carry the text.
- **R3 (N1). Fix the false sentence in the changeset.** "Every level is closed: an unknown key is refused, never dropped" (`.changeset/38048-draft-review-part.md`, the PR body and the test header) is false for the rows in `verdict.refusals` and `verdict.advisories`. Those are `RuntimeAuthoringIssueSchema`, a plain `z.object` that drops unknown keys. Keeping that behaviour is right. Change the sentence to say the five new objects are closed and the findings keep the door's own shape.
